scope: Proposed assembly process with separate rotor and carrier preparation. Steps show before/after model states, not validated insertion trajectories. The rotor is one machined body combining the measured manufacturer hub with a proposed shell, so there is no hub-to-shell joint. The sun is pressed into it. Later steps remain previewable despite unresolved earlier joints; they do not certify assembly completion.

steps.title: Start with the main housing
surfaces: Housing front mounting face
Assembly fixture locating face
steps.process: Locate the housing coaxially; establish an axial datum before installing internal subassemblies. Fixture is not modeled.
steps.check: Confirm datum, clamping distortion and access to both ends.

pathReview.reason: Fixture setup has no installation trajectory. Define housing datums and fixture access first.

steps.title: Seat ring / radial locator in main housing
surfaces: Ring mounting flange front face, z = 13.25 mm
Housing internal front seat, z = 13.25 mm
steps.process: Align the eight threaded positions on the 54 mm pitch circle. The ring, stator, winding and housing seat stay at their manufacturer positions, so the ring remains clamped by the eight front screws. The study-invented rotor shell (magnets and carrier) is what moves: it sits 4.5 mm forward to meet the stator. Insertion direction and access need checking.
steps.check: Validate locating diameter, face flatness and assembly access.

pathReview.reason: The ring flange and the stator it locates must pass the housing entry and internal shoulders. No swept-volume check or insertion-side decision exists.

steps.title: Fasten ring to main housing — eight front screws
surfaces: Screw head cones ↔ housing countersinks
Screw threads ↔ eight ring flange tapped holes
steps.process: Seat heads and tighten in a cross pattern. Thread proposal is M2.5 × 0.45; nominal penetration 3.3 mm. Torque is unspecified.
steps.check: Check thread engagement, bottoming, preload and tool clearance. Recheck screw tips if motor stack moves forward.

pathReview.reason: Each of the eight screws needs its own axis, head approach and driver access. Translating all screws from one global direction was incorrect.

steps.title: Seat prepared stator on housing shoulder, located by ring OD
steps.method: Adhesive / thermal bond; Coated sheet stacking + bonded bore; Formed insulation insertion; Wind / insert coils; Thermal attachment / lead connection; Impregnation / cure
surfaces: Stator bore 60 mm ↔ ring OD 59.96 mm (radial location, provisional bond gap)
Stator front steel face z 11.436 mm ↔ main housing annular shoulder (axial stop)
steps.process: Install the prepared 68-sheet stator over the compact ring OD until its steel end face seats against the housing shoulder at z 11.436 mm. Windings occupy z -3.3 to 12.3 mm. No long ring sleeve remains. Validate complete insertion access before animating motion.
steps.check: Choice C packaging only: 4 mm back iron, shortened radial winding region, 5.686 mm locating/bond overlap. The stator/magnet axial overlap is now the full 13.872 mm because the rotor shell moved to the stator rather than the stator moving to the rotor. Flux, winding area, bond capacity, shoulder flatness and motor alignment remain unvalidated.

pathReview.reason: Full wound-stator insertion path and tolerance stack remain unvalidated. The stack is now axially aligned with the magnet span; electromagnetic and thermal performance are still unqualified.

steps.title: Rotor bench: bond magnets into the rotor shell
surfaces: Magnet outer faces ↔ rotor shell rim bore r 40.5 mm
Magnet rear faces ↔ rotor shell closing flange, z -2.5 to -1.0 mm
Rotor shell spoked web ↔ measured hub O44.5 front face at z 0.25 mm (joint not yet defined)
Magnet side faces ↔ pole-spacing fixture
steps.process: Assemble the rotor bench part of the subassembly: the measured hub (G03), the rotor end bell (one connected solid: a six-spoke web on the hub's O44.5 front face, an outer rim carrying the magnets on its O81 bore, and a closing flange at the rear) and the magnet segments. The end bell measures O84.8 x 13.75 mm, 7482.0 mm3, one valid solid, mirroring the manufacturer arrangement where the magnet ring and the spokes are the same part. Prepare surfaces, dispense a controlled bondline and place alternating poles with tooling, then cure. Adhesive and mechanical retention are unspecified. 42 pieces are assumed; OEM magnet segmentation is unconfirmed.
steps.check: The end bell is a Primeform proposal, not OEM geometry: nothing in the source CAD joins the measured hub (O44.5 flange face) to a shell. Measured clash 0.000 mm3 against the main housing, the rear housing and the hub. STILL OPEN: the shell is joined to the hub by nothing (no fit, key, screw or bond), and the magnet band r 40.5 to 42.5 mm does not coincide with the arcuate slots in the source housings (r 41.766 to 43.236 mm), so rotor radial placement is unproven. Qualify bond thickness, temperature capability, cure and centrifugal retention, and verify polarity, spacing, concentricity and air gap.

pathReview.reason: Place magnets individually in the open rotor shell using polarity and spacing fixtures. Their placement directions and capture clearances have not been designed, and the shell itself is an unreleased Primeform proposal.

steps.title: Rotor bench: press the sun into the rotor
steps.method: Press fit: sun journal into the rotor's Ø5.95 pilot counterbore
surfaces: Sun front journal Ø6.000 mm, keyed/flat section ↔ rotor Ø5.950 counterbore, z 3.75 to 5.25 mm
Measured contact volume 0.324 mm³ over that band (0.202 mm azimuthal radius spread on the sun)
Sun rear Ø6.0 journal ↔ rotor rear Ø6 bore, z -8.75 to -6.75 mm
Rotor Ø12 front counterbore ↔ front 6701-ZZ outer race
Rotor rear Ø6 bore ↔ encoder target magnet seat
steps.process: The rotor (G03) is ONE machined body: the manufacturer hub profile with the shell's six-spoke web and pocketed magnet rim machined as part of it, 5388.4 mm³, Ø84.8 x 20.5 mm. There is no hub-to-shell joint to make. Press the sun shaft's front journal into the rotor's Ø5.95 counterbore over z 3.75 to 5.25 mm and fit both 6701-ZZ bearings into the rotor bores. The measured contact is 0.324 mm³ with a keyed/flat feature on the sun journal.
steps.check: Before release: specify the fit class, retention, runout and torque capacity of the sun-to-rotor press, and confirm the sun drive feature against hardware, because a 0.202 mm azimuthal spread measured from CAD is evidence of a key or flat, not a released specification. The rotor shows no unintended interpenetration: 0.000 mm³ against both housings, verified by cad/check_intersections.py.

pathReview.reason: A press operation needs a specified interference, a press tool and a reaction fixture, and the joint must be proven to carry the 9:1 gearbox input torque. None of those are defined yet, and the fit sits inside the rotor so the press direction and access need stating.

steps.title: Install the rotor over the stator
steps.method: Rotor subassembly / clearance review; Torque-transmitting joint unresolved
surfaces: Rotor outer wall r 42.4 mm ↔ main housing bore r 47.400 and its conical band r 44.050
Magnet inner faces r 40.5 mm ↔ stator OD r 40 mm: 0.5 mm nominal air gap
Rotor shell rear ↔ housing internal features, z -1.75 mm
steps.process: Inspect rotor subassembly outside the housing. No rotor installation route has been validated. Show the hub in its reference position. A press fit, key, spline or fasteners have not been established.
steps.check: Measured: the rotor clears the main housing and the rear housing by 0.000 mm³, and the magnets clear the stator by a 0.5 mm nominal air gap. The stator sits at its manufacturer position and the rotor shell overlaps it over the full 13.872 mm stack. Remaining: confirm the rotor radial placement, since the magnet band r 40.5 to 42.4 mm does not match the arcuate slots in the source housings (r 41.766 to 43.236 mm), and define the insertion path and tool access.

pathReview.reason: The rotor must pass over the wound stator without contacting it. The nominal air gap is 0.5 mm, so the insertion path, concentricity and any lead-in chamfer need to be stated and checked before motion is animated.

steps.title: Locate input bearings and couple sun shaft
steps.method: Bearing fits unresolved; Shaft coupling unresolved
surfaces: 6701 bearing inner races ↔ input hub journals
Bearing outer races ↔ stationary support bores (seat ownership to confirm)
Sun/input shaft coupling land ↔ input hub bore
Shaft support interfaces ↔ bearing arrangement to confirm
steps.process: Seat ownership is not established. The rear housing is shown as a receiving-part reference only, not as already installed. Decide which bearings fit to hub or housing first, and define the sun-to-hub torque connection before approving this operation.
steps.check: If an interference fit is chosen, apply force to the fitted race. Fits, preload, retention and seat geometry remain open. Resolve shaft/hub connection and retention. Tooth profile study does not validate the entire transmission.

pathReview.reason: The two bearings require individually identified seats, shoulders, fit and press-tool access. A shared axial translation cannot establish installation order. The sun shaft coupling and axial retention are undefined. Its enlarged gear and journal sections require a seat-by-seat insertion check.

steps.title: Prepare carrier: locate and retain planet pins
surfaces: Planet pin locating ends ↔ output carrier pin seats
Pin axial retention ↔ carrier faces
steps.process: Prepare the carrier subassembly with three pins; the modeled carrier lacks a validated pin retention design.
steps.check: Specify carrier bores, pin fits, shoulders and retention; verify load capacity.

pathReview.reason: Prepare pins in a separate carrier subassembly. The previous sequence showed pins mating to a carrier that was not yet installed. Pin bores and retention remain undefined.

steps.title: Fit planet supports and gears to carrier pins
steps.method: Sliding / interference fit to specify; Bearing seating + gear meshing
surfaces: Bearing or bushing inner surface ↔ planet pin OD
Outer surface ↔ planet gear bore
Planet bore ↔ bearing or bushing OD
70-tooth planet flanks ↔ 20-tooth sun and 160-tooth ring flanks
steps.process: Locate the three provisional supports on pins. Bearing versus bushing selection is still open. Align the three planets to the modeled phase before engagement. Tooth-by-tooth insertion access is unverified.
steps.check: Define diametral clearance or interference, lubrication and axial restraint. Fixed ring, sun input, carrier output gives 9:1. Backlash, root manufacture, strength and tolerance validation remain open.

pathReview.reason: Determine whether each support is assembled into the planet bore first or onto its pin first from the selected fits and access; no common path is established. Prepare planet/support/pin/carrier relationships and phase all three planets before engagement with sun and ring. Gear phase alone does not validate insertion.

steps.title: Seat output support bearings
surfaces: Bearing inner races ↔ rotating output support journals
Bearing outer races ↔ stationary housing seats (confirm each seat)
steps.process: Locate 625-ZZ and 6707-ZZ reference bearings. Identify race shoulders and retention from detailed sections.
steps.check: Specify fits, load path, axial play or preload, retention and installation force path.

pathReview.reason: Identify each bearing seat owner and shoulder before choosing installation direction and whether the bearing belongs on a shaft or in a housing first.

steps.title: Install carrier and retained planets together
steps.method: Bearing seating + gear meshing; Carrier engagement / retention unresolved
surfaces: Planet bore ↔ bearing or bushing OD
70-tooth planet flanks ↔ 20-tooth sun and 160-tooth ring flanks
Carrier planet supports ↔ pins
Carrier bearing lands ↔ output support races
steps.process: Align the three planets to the modeled phase before engagement. Tooth-by-tooth insertion access is unverified. Bring the carrier subassembly into final reference position. Pin preparation is shown separately for clarity.
steps.check: Fixed ring, sun input, carrier output gives 9:1. Backlash, root manufacture, strength and tolerance validation remain open. Carrier/pin and bearing retention require detailed design; sequence and access are not proven.

pathReview.reason: Prepare planet/support/pin/carrier relationships and phase all three planets before engagement with sun and ring. Gear phase alone does not validate insertion. Carrier insertion must move its retained pins, planet supports and planets as the chosen subassembly, not the carrier alone through them. Retention is unresolved.

steps.title: Apply lubricant and resolve closure materials
surfaces: Lubricant ↔ sun, planet and ring working flanks
Lubricant ↔ selected planet support contact surfaces
Seal ↔ designed groove and counterface (not yet defined)
Shims ↔ bearing or shoulder stack as required
steps.process: Apply the selected lubricant before closing the housing. Displayed volume is an illustrative extent. Resolve these provisions before closure; the torus shown is a placeholder, not a specified seal.
steps.check: Specify lubricant grade, dose, compatibility, life and contamination control. Define grooves, squeeze, shim stack and thread-lock locations; do not purchase from this geometry.

pathReview.reason: Apply lubricant to accessible working surfaces at the appropriate assembly stage; it is not a rigid inserted disk. Select and model actual seals, grooves, shims and locking locations before defining their operations. A generic torus does not define assembly.

steps.title: Seat rear housing on main housing
surfaces: Rear housing joint face ↔ main housing joint face
Rear housing inward wall r 29 mm over z -5.25..-4.75 mm ↔ rotor carrier web r 22.25..40.5 mm, z -5..+5 mm
Rear housing central bore ↔ rear 6701-ZZ bearing and sun rear journal
steps.process: Inspect the proposed closed position; the current rotor end bell intersects the rear housing.
steps.check: The geometric blocker is resolved: the carrier moved 4.5 mm forward, removing the 194.333 mm3 clash with the rear housing, and the rear housing does not intersect the main housing (0.000 mm3). Remaining before release: bearing seat ownership and shoulders, shim/preload, and the electrical routing that passes this joint.

pathReview.reason: No axial clash remains to block seating, but the insertion path, bearing preload and the electrical connections that pass this joint are still undefined.

steps.title: Fasten rear housing — sixteen rear screws
surfaces: Screw head cones ↔ rear housing countersinks
Screw threads ↔ main housing boss bores
steps.process: Align the rear housing and tighten in a cross pattern only after clearance redesign. Torque remains unspecified.
steps.check: Thread engagement and tightening torque are unspecified for the sixteen M2.5 x 6 screws, and no locking method is defined.

pathReview.reason: Each rear screw needs an individual axis and tool clearance after rear-housing closure is physically feasible. Current rotor/housing conflicts block this operation.

steps.title: Attach encoder target magnet to input hub

Magnet sensing face ↔ encoder sensing axis (non-contact)
steps.process: Center and retain the target magnet; adhesive or other retention must be specified.
steps.check: Validate retention, magnetic orientation, runout and encoder air gap.

pathReview.reason: Define magnet seat, retention and access on the hub before fitting the encoder board; verify sensing gap after closure.

steps.title: Mount populated driver assembly
steps.method: PCB solder assembly / capacitor mounting unresolved; PCB mounting and electrical termination unresolved
surfaces: Component terminals ↔ PCB pads
Connector leads ↔ PCB pads; connector bodies ↔ mechanical support
Encoder sensing face ↔ target magnet (non-contact)
PCB mounting holes ↔ rear support points

Encoder ↔ rotating magnet sensing gap
steps.process: Populate and reflow per a qualified PCB assembly process; connect the bulk capacitor as specified. 205 inventory designators are data-only; displayed package locations are illustrative. Mount the tested board and terminate winding/sensor leads. Board fastening details, routing and strain relief must be designed.
steps.check: Confirm footprints, solder process, pinout, capacitor mounting, power isolation and encoder alignment. No duplicate external harness is added. Check standoffs, fastener lengths, insulation, rotor clearance, connector access and encoder gap.

pathReview.reason: Populate the PCB as a separate subassembly. Components are soldered to pads, not moved through an installed board. Positions of most inventory items are unmapped. Move a populated board together with its attached components. Define standoffs, phase/sensor lead termination, strain relief and connector access first.

Cover interior ↔ driver component clearance

steps.check: Check electronics keep-out, connector openings and thermal provisions.

Screw threads ↔ receiving support holes (ownership and thread depth to confirm)
steps.process: Insert the six reference screws; verify the receiving threaded part before release.
steps.check: Torque, engagement, bottoming and PCB clearance are unspecified.
